sources.title: User-supplied brief: POST /payments, no idempotency key, ambiguous timeout

workflows.name: Payment submission

actions.name: Submit payment to provider
evidence: Provider response status code and reference stored in a response mapping field
On timeout or unexpected status, an incident is raised instead of an automatic resubmission

setupNotes: Replace the placeholder endpoint https://example.com/payments with the actual payment provider host from its API documentation before import.
Create an organization secret (e.g. PAYMENT_API_TOKEN) holding the provider's real credential; never store the value in the YAML.
Add the real payment provider domain to the HTTP allowlist before enabling this action.
Confirm the provider's actual request/response schema, auth scheme and expected status codes; the body and mapping in workflow.yaml are illustrative placeholders, not a confirmed contract.

Do not raise config.retryConfig.maxAttempts above 1 on this action until decision D-PAY-1 is resolved. Automatic retries on a non-idempotent POST /payments after an ambiguous timeout can charge the payer more than once.

No owner group is configured yet for the incident this action raises on timeout/failure. Identify who reconciles payment outcomes with the provider (decision D-PAY-3) and assign that group before publishing; provia-organization-rollout can help design it.

decisions.question: Does the payment provider support any client-side deduplication for POST /payments (a client-generated reference/order-ID field, an Idempotency-Key-style header the docs didn't mention, or an equivalent), or a status/reconciliation endpoint (e.g. GET /payments/{reference}) that can confirm whether a timed-out call actually charged the payer?
decisions.owner: Implementer, with the payment provider's integration contact

decisions.question: What is the confirmed request/response schema, authentication scheme, real endpoint host and expected success status code(s) for POST /payments?

Who should be paged when a payment submission raises an incident (ambiguous timeout / failure), and what is their reconciliation procedure with the provider (dashboard, support line, statement reconciliation)?
